record.original_question: Which projective varieties M in projective space P^n have maximum likelihood degree 1, meaning that for generic data vector (u0, u1, ..., un) the restriction of the likelihood function L(p0, p1, ..., pn) = p0^u0 · p1^u1 · ... · pn^un / (p0 + p1 + ··· + pn)^(u0 + u1 + ··· + un) to M has exactly one complex critical point after excluding singular points of M and points where L has poles or zeros?

evidence.quote: Specific Problem: Find a geometric characterization of those projective varieties whose maximum likelihood degree (ML degree) is equal to one.

The ML degree of the variety M is the number of complex critical points of the restriction of the likelihood function L to M. Here we disregard singular points of M, we only count critical points that are not poles or zeros of L, and u0, u1, . . . , un are assumed to be generic.
The corresponding likelihood function is defined as L(p0, p1, . . . , pn) = p0^u0 · p1^u1 · p2^u2 · · · · · pn^un / (p0+p1+ · · · +pn)^(u0+u1+···+un).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $M \subseteq \mathbb{P}^n$ be an irreducible complex projective variety, and consider the likelihood function
$$L(p_0,p_1,\dots,p_n) = \frac{p_0^{u_0}\, p_1^{u_1} \cdots p_n^{u_n}}{(p_0+p_1+\cdots+p_n)^{u_0+u_1+\cdots+u_n}},$$
where $u=(u_0,u_1,\dots,u_n)$ is a generic integer (or complex) data vector. The maximum likelihood degree (ML degree) of $M$ is defined as the number of complex critical points of the restriction $L|_M$, where one excludes the singular locus of $M$ and the points where $L$ has a zero or a pole (i.e., points lying on the divisor $\{p_0 p_1 \cdots p_n (p_0+\cdots+p_n)=0\}$).

Problem: Give a geometric characterization of all projective varieties $M \subseteq \mathbb{P}^n$ whose ML degree equals $1$, i.e., those varieties on which, for generic $u$, the restricted likelihood function has exactly one complex critical point.
artifact.status_search_result: June Huh (2013/2014, "Varieties with maximum likelihood degree one") established a geometric characterization: a projective variety has ML degree one if and only if it is the image of a reduced A-discriminantal variety under a monomial map with finite fibers, with the maximum likelihood estimator given explicitly by Kapranov's Horn uniformization. This resolves the question as originally posed.

status_evidence.title: Varieties with maximum likelihood degree one
status_evidence.snippet: We show that algebraic varieties with maximum likelihood degree one are exactly the images of reduced A-discriminantal varieties under monomial maps with finite fibers. The maximum likelihood estimator... is Kapranov's Horn uniformization.
status_evidence.claim: Huh provides a complete geometric characterization of projective varieties with ML degree one.

status_evidence.title: Likelihood Geometry
status_evidence.snippet: Huh-Sturmfels survey discussing ML degree one varieties and Horn uniformization.
status_evidence.claim: The characterization via Horn uniformization is recorded in the standard likelihood geometry literature.
